It also imports and syncs issues from GitHub, GitLab, Gitea and Forgejo.
help-board-view-version-control-how-it-w: Browse open and closed issues, filter by label or milestone, and open an issue to read and add to its conversation. A card counts as closed when it is archived or in a list such as Closed or Done. New issues become cards in the board's open list, and Close or Reopen moves the card between the open and closed lists. Everything is ordinary card data, so changes are kept in the board's history.
help-board-view-column-sets-what-it-is-d: Column sets let you arrange the same cards in extra ways, such as by priority, milestone or size, without moving any card out of its list. Each set has its own coloured columns.
help-board-view-column-sets-how-it-works: A board admin types a name in New column set and clicks Add, then adds columns with a name and colour. Choose a set at the top; every card is in one of its columns or in Not placed. Drag a card to another column to change its place in this set only; its list, swimlane, labels and members stay the same. Each card also shows small labels for its column in the other sets.
help-board-view-website-what-it-is-descr: The Website view shows the board as a website built from its own cards and attachments, for example a site imported from WordPress, Ghost, Blogger or a static site. A public board can open in this view, so visitors see the site at the board's address.
help-board-view-website-how-it-works-des: Cards in a list named Published are on the site, or every list's cards when there is no such list; archived cards never show. Cards in a swimlane named Pages form the menu, with subtasks as sub-pages, and the other cards are posts on the front page, newest first. A card's description is the page text and its attachments are its images and files. To use it as a public board's view, choose it in Board Settings / Board View.
help-board-view-shop-what-it-is-descript: The Shop view shows the products on the board's cards as a web shop, with pictures, prices, categories, a product page, a cart and a checkout. A card in a list on sale becomes a product when its price field has a number, and its labels become categories.
help-board-view-shop-how-it-works-descri: A board admin sets the shop up in Board Settings / Shop: the price, product code and stock fields, a private Orders list, the currency, VAT, payment methods, the lists on sale and the labels shown as categories, then ticks The shop is open. Shoppers filter by category, add products to the cart and check out. Each order becomes a new card in the Orders list, and the buyer gets a confirmation email.
help-sidebar-filter-what-it-is-descripti: The Filter shows only the cards that match what you choose, such as labels, members, assignees, dates, custom field values, card text or how long cards have been in a list. It changes no card and nobody's access, and a combination of filters can be saved under a name and used again.
help-sidebar-filter-how-it-works-descrip: Choose labels, people, dates or other conditions in the sidebar, and the board shows only the matching cards. Under Labels, OR matches any selected label and AND requires all of them; clicking a selected label again excludes it. Card text applies as you type. Closing the panel keeps the filter on until you clear it. Global Search, also here, finds cards across all your boards.
help-sidebar-search-what-it-is-descripti: Search finds the cards and lists of this board whose text contains what you type, and shows each card found on the board itself. On All Boards the same button narrows your list of boards by title.
help-sidebar-search-how-it-works-descrip: Type in the field and press Enter. The sidebar lists matching lists and cards, and the first card opens on the board with a counter under the field. Press Enter again for the next card or Shift+Enter for the previous one; the arrows do the same and wrap around. Click a card or list in the results to show it on the board, and click Search again to close the sidebar.
help-sidebar-multiselection-what-it-is-d: Multi-Selection lets you tick several cards and then do one thing to all of them at once: set a label or member, change the colour, move, copy or archive them. On All Boards it selects boards instead.
help-sidebar-multiselection-how-it-works: Turn on Multi-Selection in the board header, then tick the cards' checkboxes, or use Filter to selection in the Filter sidebar to select every card the filter shows. Choose an action in the sidebar, such as Set label for selection, Move selection or Move selection to Archive. Click Turn Multi-Selection off, the X beside the header button, when you are done. You need permission to change the board.
help-sidebar-custom-fields-what-it-is-de: Custom fields are the board's own extra fields for cards, such as a version, a budget, a customer, a checkbox or a choice from a list. A field is defined once for the board, and each card can hold its own value for it.
help-sidebar-custom-fields-how-it-works-: Click + to create a field, give it a name and a type (text, number, date, dropdown, multi-select dropdown, checkbox, currency or string template) and choose where it is shown: on the card, on the minicard, on new cards or on every card. The type cannot be changed later. Number and currency fields can show their sum at the top of each list. Card values are then filled in on the opened card.
help-sidebar-archives-what-it-is-descrip: The Archive holds the cards, lists and swimlanes that were moved to the Archive. Archiving hides something without losing it, so it can be restored later, while deleting removes it for good.
help-sidebar-archives-how-it-works-descr: Choose the Cards, Lists or Swimlanes tab and click Restore beside an item, or Restore all. A card may not be restorable while its list is archived or full under its WIP limit, and the Archive says so. Board admins also see Delete and Delete all, which cannot be undone. Archived boards are restored from the Archive page of All Boards instead.
help-sidebar-original-positions-what-it-: Original positions shows where each swimlane, list and card was put when it was made, and which of them have moved since. It is useful after a big rearrangement, or to see the title a card was created with.
help-sidebar-original-positions-how-it-w: Read the three groups, Swimlanes, Lists and Cards. Each item shows its current name, Moved when it is no longer where it was put, the place it was created in, its original title when that has changed, and when it was made. Click Refresh to read the board's history again. Items made before positions were recorded have no row.
help-sidebar-summary-what-it-is-descript: Summary is a standup report of what happened on the board, person by person, taken from the board's own records. It answers what each of us did in the last day or week, and what is overdue.
help-sidebar-summary-how-it-works-descri: Choose Last day or Last week. Each member who did something or has overdue cards gets groups for cards Done, Moved, Added and Commented, plus their Overdue cards, and each card opens from its link. Click Copy as text to copy the whole summary, ready to paste into a chat or an email.
help-sidebar-since-last-visit-what-it-is: Since your last visit lists what other people changed on this board since you last had it open: new cards, moves, comments, due date changes and members added. The menu entry shows the number of changes.
help-sidebar-since-last-visit-how-it-wor: Opening the board records your visit. Open this view to see the changes grouped by card, newest first, and click a row to open that card. Your own changes are not listed. An administrator can hide the feature in Admin Panel / Settings / Features.
help-board-visibility-what-it-is-descrip: Visibility decides who can see the board: only the people added to it (Private), every signed-in user of this WeKan (Signed-in users), or anybody with the link (Public). Editing stays with the board's members unless a board admin allows otherwise.
help-board-visibility-how-it-works-descr: A board admin clicks the visibility button in the board header and chooses Private, Signed-in users or Public; the current choice has a check mark and the button then shows the new setting. On a Signed-in users or Public board, when the administrator allows it, the admin can also tick Everyone signed in can edit. For other people the button only shows the setting.
help-board-watch-what-it-is-description: Watch sets how much you hear about this board: Watching notifies you of every change, Tracking only of changes to cards you created or are a member of, and Muted of nothing. The setting is your own; other members choose theirs.
help-board-watch-how-it-works-descriptio: Click the watch button in the board header and choose Watching, Tracking or Muted; your current level has a check mark and the button shows the new level. If the change is refused, a message says why and nothing changes. The button is hidden when an administrator has turned watching off.
help-board-sort-cards-what-it-is-descrip: Sort Cards changes the order cards are shown in inside each list: by due date, title, creation time, votes or the board's label order. It changes only what you see, and no card is moved.
help-board-sort-cards-how-it-works-descr: Click Sort Cards in the board header and choose an order; the cards in each list follow it and the button says Sort is on. Click the X beside it to remove the sort and return to the order the cards were dragged into. The choice is kept in your browser across reloads. For Label order, a board admin can change the label order with Move up and Move down when editing a label.
help-board-settings-what-it-is-descripti: Board Settings collects everything that is set for this one board: its rules, planning, colour and background, dates, views, swimlanes, lists and cards, export and import, notifications, webhooks and archive. Most entries are for board admins; your role and the site's settings decide which ones you see.
help-board-settings-how-it-works-descrip: Open the board's right sidebar with the hamburger menu and click Board Settings. Pick an entry and its own popup or page opens. The entries are grouped: rules first, then the board's look, then how it is drawn, then what goes in and out of it, and last the archive.
help-board-settings-color-what-it-is-des: Change color sets this board's own colour theme, which every member sees on this board. It is a way to tell boards apart at a glance. Only board admins can change it.
help-board-settings-color-how-it-works-d: Click a theme swatch; it is applied at once, with no Save button. For the flat and clear themes you can also pick your own colours with the colour wheels and check them in the preview. A colour you set for yourself in Member Settings still takes precedence over the board colour for you.
help-board-settings-announcement-what-it: A board announcement is a message a board admin writes for everyone on this board, shown in a bar above the board's lists. Use it for notes every member should see, such as a deadline or a change in how the board is used.
help-board-settings-announcement-how-it-: Write the text, up to 2000 characters of plain text, tick Show it to everyone on this board, and click Save. Members see the bar until they close it with its X, which hides it only for them. When the announcement is edited, it is shown again to everyone.
help-board-settings-background-what-it-i: A background image is a picture shown behind the board's lists, and also as the board's tile on the All Boards page. It can be an image address on the web or a picture uploaded and stored in WeKan.
help-board-settings-background-how-it-wo: Type an image address in Background Image URL and click Save, or use Remove Background Image to clear it. To store a picture, click Upload background image and choose a file; uploaded pictures are listed below, where clicking one makes it the board's background, and the icons download or delete it.
help-board-settings-date-what-it-is-desc: Date lets a board admin choose one date format for everyone on this board, instead of the format set for the whole site. The same popup has your own week number switch and, for board admins, calendar sync that puts the cards' due dates into a CalDAV calendar such as Nextcloud.
help-board-settings-date-how-it-works-de: Tick the board's Date Format, pick a format and click Save; untick it to follow the site setting again. A member's own enabled format in Member Settings still wins. Show week of year switches week numbers on or off for you at once. For calendar sync, enter the calendar address, user name and an app password, tick the sync box and Save.
help-board-settings-all-boards-what-it-i: All Boards Settings decides what this board's tile shows on the All Boards page, such as the card count of each list and the members' avatars. It also sets card aging, automatic archiving of untouched cards, and whether list widths are personal or shared.
help-board-settings-all-boards-how-it-wo: Tick or untick a row and it is saved at once. With card aging on, write three numbers of days after which cards fade in steps. For auto-archive, write how many days without activity a card may stay before it is archived, or leave it empty to turn that off. Templates are never archived.
help-board-settings-board-view-what-it-i: Board View chooses which views, such as Swimlanes, Lists, Table, Calendar, Gantt or the charts, are offered in this board's Board View menu, and which one the board opens in. It is set separately for when the board is public and when it is private.
help-board-settings-board-view-how-it-wo: The popup has one row per view and four checkboxes: the default view and the shown views for a public board, and the same two for a private board. Tick a view's Show box to offer it in the menu and its Default box to open the board in it.
help-board-settings-swimlane-what-it-is-: Swimlane holds the board-wide swimlane settings: whether swimlanes can be dragged, whether their height can be resized, whether all swimlanes share one row of list headers, and which Scrum fields a swimlane shows. WIP Limit Groups, shared work-in-progress limits over several lists, are also here.
help-board-settings-swimlane-how-it-work: Tick the boxes you want; the Draggable checkbox is in the table at the top. One shared list header row shows every swimlane with all of the board's lists under one header row that stays on top, without changing the lists. Click WIP Limit Groups at the bottom to add or edit shared limits.
help-board-settings-list-what-it-is-desc: List holds the board-wide list settings: whether lists can be dragged, whether their width can be resized, whether every list has the same width, and the Scrum field a list shows. It also turns on the Kanban flow policies: list policies, lists split into Doing and Done, a commitment point and a WIP limit per person.
help-board-settings-list-how-it-works-de: Tick the switches you need; the Draggable checkbox is in the table at the top. With resizing allowed, drag the handle between lists to change a width. A flow policy row appears only when that feature is turned on for the site, and once on, its details are set from each list's own menu.
help-board-settings-shop-what-it-is-desc: Shop turns the board's cards into a web shop shown in the Shop board view. A board admin chooses which custom fields are the price, product code and stock, which lists are on sale, which labels are categories, where orders are written and which payment methods are offered.
help-board-settings-shop-how-it-works-de: Set the rows and click Save; everything is saved together and checked again by the server. A card with a price in a list on sale becomes a product. Orders are written as cards to the Orders list, which must be on a private board, and the buyer can get a confirmation email. You can also make the Shop what visitors of the public board see.
help-board-settings-card-what-it-is-desc: Card decides what the minicards and the opened cards of this board show, and in what order, each independently. Use it when a board relies on a few fields, for example to put the description or the custom fields first, or to show the due date first on minicards.
help-board-settings-card-how-it-works-de: The popup has two panes, Show on Minicard and Show on Card. Tick or untick a section or a field to show or hide it, and drag rows to change their order. A few sections have their own menu with more settings, such as Subtasks and the card's dragging options.
help-board-settings-import-export-what-i: Export writes this board, or part of it, to a file: WeKan's own formats, spreadsheets, PDF, HTML, calendar files and the formats of many other tools. Import adds content from a WeKan export into this board. A board export is not a backup of the whole site.
help-board-settings-import-export-how-it: In Export, choose what to include first, then click a format and the file downloads. In Import, choose a WeKan export file in json or zip format and its content is added to this board. Import needs write access to the board, and either can be turned off by the site administrator.
help-board-settings-notifications-what-i: Notifications sets this board's defaults for email and in-app notifications, its due date reminders, email to card, and how notifications are delivered. A member's own explicit choice can still override the board default.
help-board-settings-notifications-how-it: For the in-app tray and email, pick Default to follow the site setting, or Yes or No to override it for this board. Under Due date reminders, write the days to remind on, separated by commas, where 0 is the due day and negative numbers are days after it, then click Save. The delivery sections below set what a notification carries, grouping and timing.
help-board-settings-webhooks-what-it-is-: Outgoing Webhooks send this board's activities to another service, such as a chat tool or your own integration, as they happen. Each webhook posts the activity's text together with the names and links of the board, list, swimlane, card and people involved.
help-board-settings-webhooks-how-it-work: Write a name, the address the receiving service gave you and, if it wants one, a token, choose the type and click Create. A saved webhook shows more options: which activities it sends, direct messages to card members for Mattermost, and how its messages are grouped and timed. Edit and Save it again, or use Disable This Webhook to stop it.
help-board-settings-scrum-meetings-what-: Two helpers for Scrum meetings, available to every member of the board. Daily standup is a timer that gives each member the same timebox, and Retrospective board makes a new board for a Start, Stop, Continue retrospective.
help-board-settings-scrum-meetings-how-i: Daily standup lists the board's members in a shuffled order; Start counts down the first person's time, which turns red when it runs over, and Next hands over until the last one. The timer runs only in your browser. Retrospective board creates and opens a new private board with the lists Start doing, Stop doing, Keep doing and Action items.
help-board-settings-wip-limit-groups-wha: A WIP limit group is one work-in-progress limit shared by two or more lists together, on top of each list's own limit. It is useful when work in progress spans several lists, such as Doing, Review and Testing, or when you want to cap a whole swimlane.
help-board-settings-wip-limit-groups-how: Under Add WIP limit group, tick the lists to count together, or choose a swimlane and click Apply to swimlane to tick its lists. Set the limit and click Add WIP limit group. An existing group can be changed with Apply, switched on or off with Enable WIP Limit, or removed with Delete.
help-board-settings-subtasks-what-it-is-: Subtasks split a big card into smaller cards that can each be assigned, scheduled and moved on their own, while the parent card lists them and counts how many are done. These settings decide where new subtasks are created and how a subtask shows its parent.
help-board-settings-subtasks-how-it-work: Choose how a subtask's minicard names its parent, whether the board's cards have the Subtasks section, and the board, list and swimlane new subtasks are created in. By default they go to a board of their own. Subtasks themselves are added from an opened card's Subtasks section.
help-rules-what-it-is-description: Rules automate the board: when something happens, the trigger, WeKan does something, the action. For example, when a card is moved to Done, mark it complete. Rules are made by board admins, and a board can let its members read them.
help-rules-how-it-works-description: Type a title, pick a trigger and fill in its fields, then pick an action; the rule is saved and runs from then on unless disabled. In the Workflow view you can build rules by dragging a trigger and an action. Rules can be renamed, deleted, exported and imported, and a rule can have more triggers and actions in its details.
help-member-settings-what-it-is-descript: Member Settings is your own menu, opened from your username or avatar at the top right. It has your own pages such as My Cards, Due Cards and Starred, the board overviews, and all your personal settings, from profile and password to language and fonts.
help-member-settings-how-it-works-descri: Click your username or avatar and pick an entry; its page or popup opens. What you see depends on your account type, your role and the site's settings. When a site administrator's feature profile hides some features for you, the menu says how many are hidden.
help-member-edit-profile-what-it-is-desc: Edit Profile changes how other people see you in WeKan: your full name and initials, and, when the site allows it, your username and email address. When the site allows it, you can also delete or anonymize your own account here.
help-member-edit-profile-how-it-works-de: Change the fields and click Save; the popup closes when it worked and shows the error otherwise. A username or email address already used by another account is refused, and a changed email address is marked unverified. Delete removes your account with no undo, while Anonymize account keeps your history but replaces your name.
help-member-change-settings-what-it-is-d: Change Settings holds your personal editing and display choices, such as drag handles, marking cards changed since you last opened them, the focus outline, saving editors with Enter, opening many cards at once and the checklist sound. They apply only to you, on every board.
help-member-change-settings-how-it-works: Click a switch to turn it on or off; a check mark shows it is on and it is saved at once. For Show cards count if list contains more than, type a number and click Save. Date format, week start and notifications have entries of their own in Member Settings.
help-member-change-color-what-it-is-desc: Change color sets your own colour theme for WeKan. It overrides the site theme everywhere and also the board's own colour on board pages, but only for you.
help-member-change-color-how-it-works-de: Click a theme swatch; it is applied at once. For the flat and clear themes you can choose your own colours with the colour wheels and see them in the preview. Choose Default theme to remove your choice and see the board's or the site's colours again.
help-member-change-font-what-it-is-descr: Font lets you choose the typeface, text size and text colour of the whole WeKan interface for yourself. It helps reading, for example with a larger size or a colour that suits your eyes.
help-member-change-font-how-it-works-des: Click Default or one of the font buttons; only fonts installed in your browser are offered. Choose a size and pick a text colour on the colour wheel, or click Remove to go back to the theme's colour. Changes apply at once and are saved to your profile, and the preview line shows the result.
help-member-change-avatar-what-it-is-des: Your avatar is the small picture shown for you on cards, in member lists, comments and the header. Change Avatar lets you upload pictures, choose which one is used, delete them, or go back to your initials.
help-member-change-avatar-how-it-works-d: Click Upload an avatar and pick an image; it is added to the list, and clicking its row makes it your avatar, marked with a check. Click Initials to show your initials instead. The trash icon deletes a picture after you confirm. The popup shows the size and file type limits when the site sets them.
help-member-change-password-what-it-is-d: Change Password replaces the password you sign in to WeKan with. It is for accounts with a WeKan password; accounts that sign in through another service change their password there.
help-member-change-password-how-it-works: Enter your current password, then the new password twice, and submit. The site may require a minimum length and refuse passwords that are too close to your username or email, or found in known data breaches. After the change every session of your account is signed out, and you sign in again with the new password.
help-member-passkeys-what-it-is-descript: A passkey lets you sign in with this device's fingerprint, face, screen lock or security key instead of your password. The passkey stays on your device and WeKan keeps only its public part.
help-member-passkeys-how-it-works-descri: Type a name such as My phone and click Add a passkey on this device, then confirm with your screen lock when the browser asks. Your passkeys are listed with their names and dates, and the trash icon removes one. If the browser cannot make passkeys, the popup says so.
help-member-sqrl-what-it-is-description: SQRL lets you sign in by scanning a QR code with a SQRL app, without a password. Here you add your SQRL identity to your account once, or remove it again.
help-member-sqrl-how-it-works-descriptio: Click Add my SQRL identity and a QR code appears. Scan it with a SQRL app, or click Open SQRL client for a client on this computer; the popup tells you when the identity was added, or if the code expired or failed. Remove my SQRL identity takes it off your account.
help-member-two-factor-what-it-is-descri: Two-factor authentication makes signing in ask for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone after your password, so a stolen password alone is not enough to get into your account.
help-member-two-factor-how-it-works-desc: Click Enable Two-Factor Authentication, then scan the QR code with an authenticator app or type the code shown under it into the app. Enter the 6-digit code the app shows and click Confirm and Enable. From then on signing in asks for a code, and the same popup can turn it off again unless your administrator requires it.
help-member-hidden-boards-what-it-is-des: Hidden boards lists the boards you left that you could still reach through a team, an organization or your email domain, so WeKan hid them for you instead. Leaving such a board does not change your team or organization membership.
help-member-hidden-boards-how-it-works-d: The popup shows one row per hidden board, or says there are none. Click Restore beside a board to bring it back to All Boards. This only takes it off your own hidden list; whether you may open the board is still decided by the board itself.
help-member-change-language-what-it-is-d: Change Language chooses the language of the WeKan interface for you. Your choice is saved to your profile, so it follows you to every browser. Until you choose, WeKan follows your browser's languages and falls back to English.
help-member-change-language-how-it-works: Languages are listed by their own names, with a flag, a region line for regional variants and a note for right-to-left languages; the current one has a check mark. Click a language and the interface switches at once.
help-member-invite-people-what-it-is-des: Invite People sends an email with an invitation code to people who do not have an account yet, so they can register while self-registration is off. It lets members of the organization's own email domain bring in colleagues without an administrator.
help-member-invite-people-how-it-works-d: Write the email addresses, one per line or separated by commas, tick the boards they should join when they register, and click Invite. The popup says whether the invitations were sent. You need a board role that may invite for every ticked board, and an address that already has an account stops the sending.
help-member-date-what-it-is-description: Date chooses how dates are written for you, such as year-month-day or day-month-year, with or without the time. Your own enabled format wins over the board's and the site's. The same popup sets the first day of the week and the calendar system.
help-member-date-how-it-works-descriptio: The top of the popup shows the site's and the current board's formats, so you can see what you would inherit. Tick Member Settings: Date Format and choose a format, set the week start and calendar system if you like, and click Save. Untick your format and save to follow the board or site again.
help-bookmarks-what-it-is-description: The star group in the header is your bookmarks menu: it keeps boards, other WeKan pages, and from their own menus swimlanes, lists and cards one click away. Your stars are yours alone.
help-bookmarks-how-it-works-description: Click the star to star or unstar the board or page you are on; the count shows how many you have. Click the caret or the count to open the list and click a row to go there, or See all starred items for the full Starred page. In All Boards / Starred you can unstar tiles and drag them to reorder.
help-card-similar-cards-what-it-is-descr: Similar cards lists the cards of this board whose title and description look most like this one, so a second copy of the same task is noticed before work is done twice. A very close match is marked Possible duplicate.
help-card-similar-cards-how-it-works-des: Up to five similar cards are shown here, each with the list it is in, and the heading counts them. Click one to open it. The comparison is plain text matching done by the server, without any AI service. The section can be hidden in Board Settings / Card, row Similar cards, Show on Card.
help-card-activities-what-it-is-descript: Activities is the card's own history feed: who created it, changed its title, added a label, moved it, wrote a comment or attached a file, and when. It answers what has happened to this card without asking anyone.
help-card-activities-how-it-works-descri: The newest events are listed in order, with titles, labels, comment excerpts and file names shown formatted the same way as on the card itself. Click a linked title to go to that card, list or board. A site admin can choose in Admin Panel / Settings / Security to show rich text as plain text or without clickable links.
help-card-labels-what-it-is-description: Labels are the board's coloured tags, used to group and filter cards by topic, priority or anything the team agrees on. A label can also have a due date of its own, which turns it into a lightweight milestone such as Sprint 1 or v2.0 for every card that carries it.
help-card-labels-how-it-works-descriptio: Click a label or the plus button to open the labels popup, then click labels to put them on the card or take them off; a check mark shows the chosen ones. The pencil beside a label edits its name, colour and due date, and a label with a due date shows that date next to it. Stickers and locations are in this same section.
help-card-dates-what-it-is-description: A card has four optional dates: Received for when the task arrived, Start for when work began, Due for the deadline and End for when it was finished. The due date badge is coloured by urgency and counts the days left, so late work stands out on the board.
help-card-dates-how-it-works-description: Click the plus beside a date, or the date's badge, pick the day and the time and save; a due date without a chosen time gets 17:00. Open the same popup again to change or delete it. With keyboard shortcuts on, pressing d on a card opens its due date. The card also counts how many times its due date has been changed.
help-card-members-what-it-is-description: The Members section says who is involved with the card: its members, its assignees, who created it, who requested the work and who assigned it. Requested By and Assigned By can hold board members and also a free text note, for example a name from another tracker.
help-card-members-how-it-works-descripti: Click the round plus in a row to open a list of board members and pick people; they are shown as avatars or initials, and clicking an avatar again removes them. Under Requested By and Assigned By, the Add link below the plus writes the free text instead. Which rows appear is chosen in Board Settings / Card.
help-card-fields-what-it-is-description: The Card section holds the card's own working fields, such as its dependencies, blocked state, class of service, priority scores, its sorting number and its card buttons. An opened card shows every field the board has chosen to show on cards, empty or not, ready to be filled in.
help-card-fields-how-it-works-descriptio: Fill in or change a field directly in this section. What appears here, in which section and in what order is decided for the whole board in Board Settings / Card, in the Show on Card pane: tick or untick a row, or drag it to reorder. The minicard follows the Show on Minicard pane the same way.
help-card-time-what-it-is-description: Time tracking records how many hours have been spent on the card, with an optional estimate, Billable and Overtime flags and a day by day log of who worked how long. The total feeds the board's time, workload and billing views, and the Flowtime and Pomodoro timers here add to it.
help-card-time-how-it-works-description: Click the time badge or the hamburger beside Spent time to open Change spent time, enter the hours (decimals allowed), optionally an estimate and the flags, and Save. Under Time by day, pick a date, enter hours and a note and click Log time; you can remove your own entry until it is approved or invoiced. The badge turns red when Overtime is ticked.
help-card-custom-fields-what-it-is-descr: Custom fields are the board's own extra fields for its cards, beside the built-in ones: a version, a budget, a customer, a checkbox or a choice from a list. They are defined once for the board, and each card can then carry its own value.
help-card-custom-fields-how-it-works-des: Here you choose which of the board's custom fields this card uses and fill in their values. New fields are created in Board Settings / Card, in the Custom Fields section, by choosing a name and a type such as Text, Number, Date, Dropdown, Checkbox or Currency. A field can be shown on the minicard too, and number fields can be summed at the top of each list.
help-card-planning-poker-what-it-is-desc: Planning Poker lets the team estimate a card together. Everybody picks a value from the deck without seeing the others' picks, and when the vote ends WeKan shows who chose what and which value won, so the estimate is agreed rather than guessed by one person.
help-card-planning-poker-how-it-works-de: Open the section's hamburger, Edit Planning Poker, optionally allow all logged in users and set an end time, and Save. Each voter clicks one value; clicking another changes the vote. A board admin clicks Finish to see the results, types a number and clicks Set Estimation. Replay clears the votes for a new round.
help-card-scrum-what-it-is-description: Scrum settings holds the card's place in the board's Scrum planning: its sprint and past sprints, release, issue type, acceptance criteria and backlog rank. The card can also be marked as a Story or a Task, which the sprint and backlog views use.
help-card-scrum-how-it-works-description: Open Edit under the fields to change them and Save; only those who may change the card can edit. The hamburger in the section heading picks the card kind: none, Story or Task. Sprints themselves are planned, started and closed in the board's Scrum views, and which of these fields show is set in Board Settings / Card.
help-card-description-what-it-is-descrip: The description is the card's main text: the details of the task, notes, links or pasted meeting notes. It is written in Markdown, so it can have headings, lists, links, emoji and images while staying plain text to edit.
help-card-description-how-it-works-descr: Click the description to edit it in a plain text box. Type the at sign and the start of a name to get member suggestions. Save, and the text is shown formatted. Uploaded files stay in the Attachments section and can be referred to from the text.
help-card-checklists-what-it-is-descript: A checklist is a list of items on the card, each ticked off when done, for steps, acceptance criteria or a routine. A card can have several, and the minicard can show how many items are done.
help-card-checklists-how-it-works-descri: Add a checklist with its plus, then add items and tick them as they are done. Each checklist's own hamburger has its actions: edit all items at once as text, export or import, move or copy it, check or uncheck all items, hide checked items, set an automatic reset that unchecks everything on a daily, weekly or monthly schedule, or delete it. A checklist can also have its own deadline.
help-card-subtasks-what-it-is-descriptio: Subtasks split a big card into smaller cards that can each be assigned, scheduled and moved on their own, while this parent card lists them and counts how many are done. A subtask is an ordinary card, kept on the board chosen for subtasks.
help-card-subtasks-how-it-works-descript: Click the plus, type a title and Save to create a subtask; tick Inherit parent's labels to copy this card's labels onto it. The link icon adds an existing card as a subtask instead. Each subtask's hamburger has View it, Go to Board and, for board admins, Delete. Click a subtask's title to rename it.
help-card-attachments-what-it-is-descrip: Attachments are files kept with the card: documents, images, videos, logs or archives. An image can also become the cover picture shown on the minicard.
help-card-attachments-how-it-works-descr: Click the plus to add files from your computer, paste or drop an image, attach another card, or draw a new picture. Any size limit and allowed file types are shown under these choices. Click an attachment to open it in the slideshow, and use the buttons beside it to download, rename or delete it; its hamburger has the cover image choices.
help-card-comments-what-it-is-descriptio: Comments are the card's discussion: questions, answers, updates and decisions, kept with the work they are about. A comment can answer an earlier one, and the answer is shown under it as a thread.
help-card-comments-how-it-works-descript: Write in the comment field, using Markdown and mentioning people with the at sign, and post it. Click Reply beside a comment to answer it; an In reply to banner shows what you are answering, and closing it makes a normal comment. You can edit or delete your own comments, and on some boards only a comment's author may change it.
help-card-stickers-what-it-is-descriptio: Stickers are small icons put on a card, such as a thumbs up, a bug, a clock or a trophy, to mark it at a glance without using a label or a colour. They are shown both on the minicard and in the opened card.
help-card-stickers-how-it-works-descript: Click a sticker in the picker to add it to the card; a check mark shows it is on the card, and clicking it again takes it off. In the card, the small cross beside a sticker removes it. Adding and removing needs the right to change the card.
help-card-locations-what-it-is-descripti: A card can have several locations, the places where the work happens, such as a customer's office, a site or a venue. Each has a name, an address and, when known, coordinates with an Open in map link.
help-card-locations-how-it-works-descrip: Fill in the location name, address, latitude and longitude and click Save. Pasting a map link lets the popup detect the place for you, so nobody has to type coordinates. Clicking a location on the card opens it again to change or delete it, and the cross beside it removes it at once.
help-card-dependencies-what-it-is-descri: Dependencies link this card to other cards: it blocks, is blocked by, fixes, duplicates or relates to them. With dependencies turned on in Member Settings, they are drawn as coloured arrow lines across the board, so the order of work is visible at a glance.
help-card-dependencies-how-it-works-desc: Choose the relation type and a colour, then search and click the card to link to. The link is shown in the card's Dependencies and as a line on the board. Click a line, or use the card's Dependencies, to change its type, colour or icon, or to remove it. You can also drag a minicard's connect handle onto another card.
help-card-action-items-what-it-is-descri: Action items turn the to-do lines of pasted meeting notes into cards. Lines such as TODO: Book the venue, an unticked task line, or a line starting with a mention are found by their shape, without AI.
help-card-action-items-how-it-works-desc: The popup lists the cards that would be made, each with a tick and the member a mention points to. Untick what you do not want and click Create. The new cards go into the same list as this card and link back to it. A mention becomes a member only when that person is an active member of the board.
help-card-history-what-it-is-description: History is the list of every change made to this card: who changed what, when, and from which value to which. Any change can be picked and restored, so a mistake can be undone even later.
help-card-history-how-it-works-descripti: Type in Search to narrow the rows, or click a person's avatar to see only their changes. Page with the arrows. Tick one or more rows and click Restore; several rows are restored oldest first as one change, which can itself be undone. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y also undo and redo your own last change.
help-card-qr-code-what-it-is-description: The QR code shows this card's link as a code you can scan, to open the card on a phone or tablet without typing its address. It changes nothing on the card.
help-card-qr-code-how-it-works-descripti: Point the phone's camera at the code and open the link; the address is also shown as text below it. The code is drawn in your browser and nothing is sent anywhere. Whoever scans it still has to sign in and have access to the board. A link that is too long for a QR code is reported instead.
help-card-move-what-it-is-description: Move Card moves the card to another place on this board or to another board. It does what dragging does, also where dragging cannot reach, such as another board or an exact spot in a long list.
help-card-move-how-it-works-description: Choose the board, swimlane and list, then a card and whether to go above or below it. You can change the title, write an optional move reason, and tick Leave a link at the original location to keep a linked card where it was. Click Done once the destination has loaded. Shift+M opens this popup too, and the destination is remembered per board.
help-card-copy-what-it-is-description: Copy Card makes a new, independent copy of the card on this board or another one, with its own number and its own copies of the comments, checklists, attachments and subtasks.
help-card-copy-how-it-works-description: Edit the title if you like; an empty title copies nothing. Choose the board, swimlane and list, then a card and whether the copy goes above or below it, and click Done. If the copy is refused, the reason is shown here. Shift+C opens this popup too, and the destination is remembered per board.
help-card-recurrence-what-it-is-descript: Card recurrence makes WeKan create a fresh copy of this card in the same list on a schedule, for recurring work such as a weekly status report or a monthly invoice that would otherwise be recreated by hand.
help-card-recurrence-how-it-works-descri: Pick Daily, Weekly or Monthly, or Off to stop it; Off is the default. The server then makes the copies by itself, with no other setup needed. Archiving the card also stops it from making more copies, even if the interval is still set.
help-card-copy-many-what-it-is-descripti: Copy Template to Many Cards makes several copies of this card at once. The card works as a template: its checklists, attachments, labels and other fields go to every copy, and only the title and description differ.
help-card-copy-many-how-it-works-descrip: In the text box, write one entry per card with its title and description, following the example already filled in. Choose the board, swimlane, list and the place beside a card, then click Done. If the text is not in the right format, nothing is created and the error is shown here.
help-card-color-what-it-is-description: Set color gives the card a background colour of its own so it stands out on the board, for example red for urgent work or a customer's own colour. The card's text is made readable on the colour automatically.
help-card-color-how-it-works-description: Click one of the named colours, a custom colour already used on this board, or pick any colour under Custom color, then click Save. Remove takes the colour away. The colour shows on the minicard and in the opened card, unless turned off in Board Settings / Card.
help-card-drawing-what-it-is-description: Drawing lets you draw or write by hand on the card with a mouse, a finger or a pen: a sketch, a diagram, a signature or a handwritten note. The drawing stays editable and its picture is also saved as an attachment of the card.
help-card-drawing-how-it-works-descripti: Pick a colour and a line width and draw. Undo steps back, the Eraser removes the lines it touches and Clear removes all. Save keeps the lines on the card and stores the picture as an attachment; a new drawing becomes the card's cover image. Saved drawings are listed here to open and edit again, and Download as SVG saves one as a file.
help-card-more-what-it-is-description: More shows the card's link, its parent cards and when it was created. It is where the card is made a subtask of another card, and where a board admin deletes the card for good.
help-card-more-how-it-works-description: Copy card link to clipboard copies the card's address. Under Change card's parent, choose a source board and a parent card, or none to make it a top-level card again; Add another parent card adds more parents, and the cross beside one removes it. Delete, for board admins only, removes the card permanently after a confirmation.
help-card-create-board-what-it-is-descri: Create board from this card turns the card into a link to a new board. It is for a card that has grown into a project of its own: the work moves to its own board, and the card stays where it was as the way into it.
help-card-create-board-how-it-works-desc: The new board's name is filled in with the card's title; change it if you like and press Create board from this card. The board is created with you as its admin, and the card then opens that board. Nothing else on the card changes. If it is refused, the reason is shown and nothing changes.
help-card-link-to-board-what-it-is-descr: Link to board puts a linked card of this card on another existing board. The card then shows on both boards: the original stays where it is, and the link shows its content where you put it.
help-card-link-to-board-how-it-works-des: Choose the board, swimlane and list, then a card and whether the link goes above or below it, and click Done. In an empty list the link goes to the bottom. The original card is not changed, and the labels are not copied. The destination is remembered per board.
help-card-actions-what-it-is-description: The card's hamburger menu, Card Actions, collects everything you can do with the card as a whole, rather than with one of its fields. Which entries appear depends on your role on the board.
help-card-actions-how-it-works-descripti: Move and copy has Move Card, Copy Card, Save as Template, Copy Template to Many Cards, Card recurrence and moving to the top or bottom of the list. Then come Watch and Star, and Appearance with Set color, Drawing and Create cards from action items. Share has the card link, Link to board, QR code and History, then Export and Import. Archive has Archive card, More and Create board from this card.
help-admin-version-what-it-is-descriptio: The Version pane shows what this WeKan is running: the WeKan version and how it was installed, the operating system, Meteor, the database and Node.js. It is the first pane of Admin Panel / Settings and the information to copy into a bug report when asking for help.
help-admin-version-how-it-works-descript: Read the table, which is grouped into Platform, OS, Meteor, Database and Node. Press Check Version to compare with the newest released WeKan, FerretDB, Meteor, Node and NPM versions; while it runs it says it is loading, and if the check fails you see one failure message instead.
help-admin-appearance-what-it-is-descrip: Appearance decides how this WeKan looks and what All Boards shows: hidden parts such as public boards or board activities, who may create boards, the date format, how wide card details open, link addresses, the external issue tracker autolink, the product name, colours and logos.
help-admin-appearance-how-it-works-descr: Change the fields of one group and press that group's own Save, which stores only that group. Ticks under All Boards: Hide mean the thing is hidden, except boards every signed-in user can edit, which is ticked when allowed. Change color saves without a Save button and is the only group an organization's own admin sees.
help-admin-features-what-it-is-descripti: Features is where a site administrator turns optional parts of WeKan on or off for the whole instance: board views, helpers, Kanban and Scrum tools, card fields, Workload and capacity, Budget and billing, SQRL, ActivityPub, read-only Rules and the optional compatible APIs. Swimlanes and lists are always there.
help-admin-features-how-it-works-descrip: Untick what this WeKan should not offer, including card fields no board should show, and press Save. An unticked feature disappears from everyone's interface and the server refuses it too, but its data is kept. You can require approval for features that a WeKan update adds, and name pilot users who still see features that are off.
help-admin-feature-profiles-what-it-is-d: A feature profile gives chosen users, teams or organizations a smaller WeKan by hiding some optional features from them, while everybody else keeps seeing everything. It can hide the same features the Features pane can switch off.
help-admin-feature-profiles-how-it-works: Press Add profile, give it a name, tick the features it hides and list its users, teams and organizations, then press the pane's Save. Names that matched nobody are reported after saving and are not stored. Profiles are tried in page order, and the user's member menu tells them which profile hides how many features.
help-admin-security-what-it-is-descripti: Security holds server-wide switches for what rich text may do and what may be imported or exported. Use them to stop clickable links, show all formatted text as plain source, block imports or exports, limit the import size, leave out avatars, or replace real user identities with anonymous names.
help-admin-security-how-it-works-descrip: Tick a switch and it is saved at once; the largest import size is saved when you leave the field, and an empty value means no limit. Every switch is off by default and is enforced by the server, so a turned-off import or export is refused even if someone calls it directly.
help-admin-activities-what-it-is-descrip: Three server-wide switches for sites that must limit activity tracking: stop recording who did what, stop sending notifications about activities, or stop users from watching boards, lists and cards.
help-admin-activities-how-it-works-descr: Tick a switch and it is saved at once. With activities off, nothing new is recorded and existing entries are no longer shown. With notifications off, no in-app, email or other notifications are sent. With watch off, nobody can change a watch level. Untick to turn it back on; activities not recorded meanwhile do not come back.
help-admin-delete-what-it-is-description: Deleting in WeKan normally only marks lists, cards and attachments as deleted so they can be restored. This pane holds the one switch that lets a site administrator destroy such content for good.
help-admin-delete-how-it-works-descripti: Tick Enable permanent delete for Global Admin; it saves at once and deletes nothing by itself. Delete icons then appear where permanent delete is offered, such as a list in the recycle bin or an archived board in the All Boards archive. Every setting change and permanent delete attempt is recorded in Recovery. Untick it when you are done.
help-admin-announcement-what-it-is-descr: A site-wide banner for telling every signed-in user something at once, such as a maintenance break, a new address or a policy change. It is separate from a board's own announcement.
help-admin-announcement-how-it-works-des: Tick Active System-Wide Announcement, type the message and press Save. The banner appears at the top of Home, All Boards and the boards users are members of. A user can close it, and it stays closed for them until you change the text. Untick the checkbox to take it down for everybody.
help-admin-accessibility-what-it-is-desc: The accessibility page is where this WeKan tells its users how accessible it is and whom to contact about a barrier. This pane turns that page on and sets its title and content.
help-admin-accessibility-how-it-works-de: Tick Accessibility page enabled, which saves at once, then write the title and content and press Save. The content is formatted like a card description. Board members then find an Accessibility link in the board's right sidebar. Untick it to hide the link again.
help-admin-translation-what-it-is-descri: Custom translation strings override WeKan's built-in texts on this instance, per language, for example to use your organization's own word for board or to correct a string before a fixed translation arrives.
help-admin-translation-how-it-works-desc: Press New, choose the language, enter the key of the string to replace (not the English sentence) and the text to show instead, then Save. Only the translation text of an existing row can be edited, and a row can be deleted from its menu. The overrides apply to text the server makes, such as emails; in the browser they currently show only for site administrators.
help-admin-pwa-what-it-is-description: The PWA pane controls what browsers and phones read about WeKan itself: extra meta and link tags in every page, the web manifest used when WeKan is installed as an app, and the Android app links file that lets an Android app open WeKan links.
help-admin-pwa-how-it-works-description: Tick the part you want to customize, which saves at once, paste your tags or JSON and press Save. Invalid JSON is refused and nothing is saved. Meta tags are added only as meta elements, so scripts, styles and page-refreshing tags are dropped. With a switch off, WeKan uses its built-in defaults.
help-admin-global-webhooks-what-it-is-de: Global webhooks send a message to another address, such as a chat or an automation server, whenever something happens on any board of this WeKan. They use the same form as a board's own webhooks. The pane also lists the internal hosts webhooks may reach and the login and registration webhook.
help-admin-global-webhooks-how-it-works-: Fill in the empty form with a name, the address, an optional token and the type, one-way or two-way, and press Create. On a saved webhook you can disable it, choose which activities it sends and how it delivers, then Save. List hosts on WeKan's own network under Internal destinations, one per line, so webhooks are allowed to reach them.
help-admin-shared-labels-what-it-is-desc: Shared labels give a label one name and one colour on many boards at once: on every board, on the boards of an organization, or on the boards of a team. Use them for labels such as Urgent or Customer that should look the same everywhere.
help-admin-shared-labels-how-it-works-de: Add a label in the last row with a name, colour and catalog, then press Add shared label; each row saves or deletes on its own. On a card's labels, board members see the shared labels their board may use and click one to add it. Renaming or recolouring here changes it on every board, and deleting it leaves it on those boards as their own label.
help-admin-email-what-it-is-description: The E-mail pane sets how WeKan sends mail, either through the server's own mail settings or through a provider configured here, and holds related settings: which email domain may invite people when self-registration is off, whether users may change their address, what to do with bounced mail, and the invite and activity email templates.
help-admin-email-how-it-works-descriptio: Tick Enable below email settings, choose SMTP or a built-in provider, fill in its username, password and sender address and press Save; a saved password is kept when the field is left blank. Send a test email to yourself to check it works. Without the tick, the server's own mail settings stay in use. Empty template fields keep the built-in emails.
help-admin-notifications-what-it-is-desc: The site-wide default for notifications: whether the in-app notification tray and email are on or off for everyone, and how email, the tray and outgoing webhooks deliver by default. Board settings and each member's own settings can override it for their own scope.
help-admin-notifications-how-it-works-de: Choose Yes or No for Notification tray and for Email; the choice saves at once. Open a channel to set its layout, what it shows, how notifications are grouped and when they are sent, each saved at once. Board admins and members can pick Default to fall back to what you set here. The email-to-card settings are in the same pane.
help-admin-domains-what-it-is-descriptio: Domains lists every email domain used by accounts on this WeKan, with how many users each has. It is a quick way to see which organizations are on the instance and to spot an unexpected domain without reading the whole user list.
help-admin-domains-how-it-works-descript: Read the table, one row per domain with its user count. Type part of a domain in the search box and press Enter to find it, and move between pages with the previous and next buttons. Nothing is stored; the table is counted fresh each time it is shown.
help-admin-organizations-what-it-is-desc: Organizations group users by company, department or customer so boards and template boards can be shared with all of them, their members can be kept in step with a directory such as LDAP, and, with multitenancy, an organization can have its own domains, branding and admins.
help-admin-organizations-how-it-works-de: Click New in the first column's header to create one, Edit to change a row, and the row menu to delete it or appoint organization admins. Row switches for shared templates, adding members to boards and syncing members from the login provider save at once. Tick Add board members only from the same Organization to limit who can be added to boards.
help-admin-teams-what-it-is-description: Teams group users who work together so a board or template boards can be shared with the whole team, members can be kept in step with a directory such as LDAP, and the People list can be narrowed to one team. They work like organizations without the tenant part.
help-admin-teams-how-it-works-descriptio: Click New in the first column's header to create a team, Edit to change it, or the row menu to delete it. Row switches save at once. To put people into teams, tick them in Admin Panel / People / People and click Teams. Tick Add board members only from the same Team to limit who can be added to boards.
help-admin-people-what-it-is-description: People lists every account on this WeKan with its email, admin status, feature profile, active state, sign-in countries, lock status, last activity and creation date. It is where you create, edit, deactivate, unlock, impersonate, anonymize and delete accounts.
help-admin-people-how-it-works-descripti: Search by username, name or email and press Enter, and narrow with Show and Team. Click New to create a user and Edit to change one. Click the active sign to deactivate or activate, and the red lock or Unlock All to unlock. The row menu has impersonate, anonymize and delete; tick several people and click Teams to change their teams.
help-admin-locked-users-what-it-is-descr: Brute force protection locks an account after too many failed sign-ins. This pane sets how many failures trigger a lockout, how long it lasts and the time window in which failures are counted, separately for existing usernames and for usernames that do not exist.
help-admin-locked-users-how-it-works-des: Fill in the failures, lockout period and window, in seconds, for known and unknown users and press Save; the new values apply at once without a restart. To see and release locked accounts, open Admin Panel / People / People, choose Locked Users Only and click a red lock, or Unlock All.
help-admin-audit-log-what-it-is-descript: The audit log is the trail of what site administrators did, newest first: when, who, which action, whether it succeeded, its details and the address it came from. It answers who changed something and when for people, login, storage and backup settings.
help-admin-audit-log-how-it-works-descri: Read the table of When, Administrator, Action, Details and IP; a refused action is marked with its error. Type in the search box to narrow the rows by administrator, action or details, and use the arrows under the table to move between pages.
help-admin-roles-what-it-is-description: Roles decides which board roles may invite people to a board, lets you build custom roles from what a board member may do, and shows what every role may do. Site administrators always have every right.
help-admin-roles-how-it-works-descriptio: Under Allow Invite to Board, tick the roles that may invite and press Save. Under Custom roles, type a name, tick what the role may do and press Add role; each row saves or deletes on its own, and board admins can then give the role to members. The Roles Status table shows the result of your ticks, even before you save.
help-admin-shared-templates-what-it-is-d: Shared templates lets you browse users' shareable template boards by organization, team or email domain. The ticks also decide which kinds of group a template board may be shared with from All Boards / Templates.
help-admin-shared-templates-how-it-works: Tick Organizations, Teams or Domains; each tick saves at once for the whole instance. Under each ticked scope you see every group, its users and their template boards, and clicking a template board opens it. Whether one group's templates reach its members is set per organization and team in their own panes.
help-admin-login-what-it-is-description: Login decides what is allowed at sign-in, such as forgot password, self-registration, username change, deleting one's own account and the method selector. It also lets you override the server's login settings without a restart, for example password login, the default method, session length, automatic logout, password rules and compulsory two-factor authentication.
help-admin-login-how-it-works-descriptio: Tick or untick the Login: Allow checkboxes; each saves on click. With self-registration off, use Invite People to invite addresses to chosen boards. In the settings form each field says which value is in effect; type or choose a value and save, or leave it empty or choose Default to fall back to the server's settings. Each login method has its own pane in the People menu.
help-admin-saml-what-it-is-description: SAML login lets people sign in through your organization's identity provider instead of a WeKan password. The provider confirms who they are with a signed message and WeKan signs them in, creating the account at the first login.
help-admin-saml-how-it-works-description: Enter the identity provider's sign-in address and signing certificate, this WeKan's issuer name and the other options in this pane, or in the server's settings; a value saved here wins over the server's. Once enabled, the sign-in page shows a Sign In with SAML button that takes the user to the identity provider and back.
help-admin-ldap-what-it-is-description: LDAP login lets people sign in with the username and password they already have in your directory, such as Active Directory or OpenLDAP. WeKan checks the password against the directory, creates the account at the first login and can keep names, emails, admin status, organizations and teams in step with the directory.
help-admin-ldap-how-it-works-description: Fill in the directory's address, port, encryption, base and how users are searched, then save; a saved value wins over the server's settings and Default gives the server's value back. Press Test LDAP Connection to try the settings in effect, and Sync LDAP users now to run the background sync at once. Choose LDAP as the default method in the Login pane.
help-admin-oauth2-what-it-is-description: OAuth2 and OpenID Connect login lets people sign in with an account at another service, such as Keycloak, Authelia or GitLab, instead of a WeKan password. Unlike the fixed social login providers, you point it at any provider by giving its addresses.
help-admin-oauth2-how-it-works-descripti: Register WeKan as an application at the provider, then enter its client id, secret, server address, endpoints and how its user fields map to WeKan here; a value saved here wins over the server's settings and applies at the next login without a restart. The sign-in page then shows a sign-in button whose text is set in the Login pane.
help-admin-cas-what-it-is-description: CAS is a single sign-on system: people log in once on your organization's CAS server, and WeKan trusts the ticket it gives back, so WeKan never sees the password.
help-admin-cas-how-it-works-description: Enter the CAS server's base, login and validation addresses here and turn it on; a value saved here wins over the server's settings. Choose CAS as the default method in the Login pane, or let users pick it from the method selector. Signing in takes the browser to the CAS login page and back to WeKan, signed in.
help-admin-header-login-what-it-is-descr: Header login lets a trusted reverse proxy that already did single sign-on tell WeKan who the user is, so the user is signed in without a password and the account is created at the first visit.
help-admin-header-login-how-it-works-des: These settings are shown read-only here and cannot be saved from the Admin Panel, because a trusted proxy can sign in as anybody; they are set in the server's settings with a restart. The proxy must authenticate the user, send the identity headers and remove any such headers sent by clients, and only the listed proxy addresses are trusted.
help-admin-oauth-providers-what-it-is-de: These are the ready-made social login buttons: Google, GitHub, Facebook, Twitter, Meteor Developer, Weibo and Meetup. Each needs only the app id and secret the provider gives you, and they can be used alongside the generic OAuth2 login.
help-admin-oauth-providers-how-it-works-: Create an app on the provider's developer site with WeKan's callback address, then enter its id and secret here and turn the provider on; a value saved here wins over the server's settings. A Sign in with button for that provider then appears on the sign-in page.
help-admin-passwordless-what-it-is-descr: Passwordless login lets a user sign in with a one-time code that WeKan emails them, instead of a password. It is a convenience for people who forget passwords, not a second factor, and is only as safe as the user's mailbox.
help-admin-passwordless-how-it-works-des: Make sure outgoing email works, then turn it on here; a value saved here wins over the server's settings. The sign-in page then offers to email a sign-in code: the user types their address, receives a code valid for a short time, enters it and is signed in.
help-admin-backup-what-it-is-description: Backup takes an archive of this WeKan now or on a schedule, with the text data, attachments and avatars as separate choices, and restores it. A site administrator backs up the whole instance or one organization; an organization's own admin backs up only its boards. Continuous backup instead streams every change so you can restore to any moment.
help-admin-backup-how-it-works-descripti: Choose the scope, tick what to include and press Backup now; a complete backup needs all three and the whole instance. Set a daily, weekly or monthly schedule and Save. Press List backups and restore one, either adding only missing data or replacing everything. In Continuous backup, set the target folder, contents and retention, then pick a restore point.
help-admin-attachments-what-it-is-descri: The Attachments panes decide where card attachments and avatars are stored, how big they may be, how long they are kept and how they move between storages. Files can be kept on the server's disk, in the database or in cloud storage such as S3, MinIO, Azure, Google Cloud Storage or WebDAV.
help-admin-attachments-how-it-works-desc: Pick a pane from the left menu. Set the storage new files go to, configure each storage with its own read and write switches, and move attachments or avatars from one storage to another. Limits sets upload and download sizes, Retention deletes old attachments after a number of days, and Database migration moves text data between MongoDB and FerretDB.
help-admin-problems-summary-what-it-is-d: The first page of Admin Panel / Problems and your daily check of the whole server. It tells you what is running right now, what is wrong right now, and how many new problems each report has collected, with the buttons to fix or acknowledge them.
help-admin-problems-summary-how-it-works: Status lists migrations and repairs in progress, which can slow logins, followed by each problem with a count and what to do, and a Repair broken cards, Restore or Repair button where one applies. A repair that deletes data asks you to click Confirm first. Under Data health, Start runs a background scan. Under Problems, tick the reports you have reviewed and press Acknowledge to reset their new count, or Clear to delete their rows.
help-admin-problems-security-what-it-is-: Every attempt that a security guard refused or noticed: what it was, how severe, who tried it, from where and how many times. It shows that somebody tried, not only that the hole is closed. The security switches themselves are in Admin Panel / Settings / Security.
help-admin-problems-security-how-it-work: Rows are listed newest first, and a repeated attempt is one row whose Attempts count grows, while Detail says what the guard saw. Type a name, category, source, username or address in the search box to filter as you type, and click a username to open that account. Acknowledge or clear the report on Problems / Summary.
help-admin-problems-impersonation-what-i: The audit trail of administrators acting as other users. Impersonation lets an administrator see WeKan the way one user sees it, for example to export a private board, and this report keeps that power visible afterwards.
help-admin-problems-impersonation-how-it: A row is written when an administrator chooses Impersonate user in Admin Panel / People, creates a login token for another user through the REST API, or exports a board, card or attachment while impersonating. Each row shows the date, the administrator, the impersonated user, the board and the reason, newest first. Click a name to open that user, and search with Enter. Nothing here changes or deletes a row.
help-admin-problems-password-length-what: Shows who signs in with a password shorter than the minimum length, from where, and whether they have changed it since. You can see who would be affected before you enforce a minimum for new passwords.
help-admin-problems-password-length-how-: Set the Minimum password length, tick Enforce the minimum length to refuse shorter new passwords, and press Save. Sign-in is never refused, but with enforcement on, an account with an old short password is asked to change it first. The table has one row per account with first and last login, addresses, the login count and when it was fixed. Filter by Too short password, Fixed to long enough password or All. Accounts that sign in through LDAP, OAuth2, OIDC, SAML, CAS or Sandstorm are not listed.
help-admin-problems-performance-what-it-: Explains how WeKan loads the cards of a board, which decides how much a big board costs to open. It is a description only, with nothing to click or save.
help-admin-problems-performance-how-it-w: Card loading is automatic for each board: a board with more than 500 cards loads only the cards visible in each list as you scroll, with counts from the server, and a smaller board loads every card. A server operator can force all or lazy loading, or change the card count, in the server's settings and then restart. A board's Statistics view shows which mode it uses.
help-admin-problems-speed-what-it-is-des: Lists the web page and REST API requests that took too long to answer, so you can see which pages or calls are slow and how often.
help-admin-problems-speed-how-it-works-d: Every request except static files is timed, and one that takes two seconds or longer by default is recorded. The same slow request is kept as one row whose count and date go up, and Detail shows the method, the path and how long it took. Search filters as you type, and Problems / Summary acknowledges or clears it. The limit, or turning it off, is set in the server's settings. Live call times of methods and publications are under Instrumentation instead.
help-admin-problems-tests-what-it-is-des: Self-checks of the running server that failed. Shortly after start, WeKan checks that the database answers, that the files directory can be written, that the memory heap has room left and that the disk has free space.
help-admin-problems-tests-how-it-works-d: The checks run once, about 15 seconds after the server starts, and only a failure makes a row: Source names the check and Detail gives its error message. No new problems means nothing has failed since the report was last cleared. The pane has no button to run them again, so restart WeKan. Acknowledge or clear it on Problems / Summary.
help-admin-problems-cpu-what-it-is-descr: Watches the processor load of the whole machine, because WeKan and its database on the same computer can use enough CPU to slow other software. Periods of sustained high CPU are recorded here, and long operations slow down while the machine is busy.
help-admin-problems-cpu-how-it-works-des: The top line shows the current CPU usage, the number of cores, the load average, the recent minimum, average and maximum, and what WeKan is doing, refreshed every 5 seconds. The table below lists past busy periods: a start row, at most one row about slowing down, and an end row with the duration, the peak and whether slowing down helped. Search filters as you type. Thresholds, or turning the monitor off, are in the server's settings.
help-admin-problems-ram-what-it-is-descr: Watches how much memory and swap the whole machine uses, and records when a period of high memory use starts and when it ends. Running out of memory, or swapping, slows or crashes WeKan and other software on the same machine.
help-admin-problems-ram-how-it-works-des: The line at the top shows current memory use as a percentage and as used and total gigabytes, plus swap when the machine has any, refreshed every 5 seconds. Below it, the table holds one start row and one end row for each high-memory period, newest first, 10 rows a page, with a search box. Acknowledge or clear it on Problems / Summary. The limits are in the server's settings and are read when the server starts.
help-admin-problems-disk-what-it-is-desc: Watches free space on the disks that hold the database, attachments and uploads. A full disk makes uploads fail and stops the database from writing, so this gives an early warning before that happens.
help-admin-problems-disk-how-it-works-de: One live line per disk shows the percentage used, free and total gigabytes, its location and what WeKan keeps there, refreshed every 30 seconds, and a disk in a high period is highlighted. The table below has a start row and an end row for each period of high use, and search filters as you type. Acknowledge or clear it on Problems / Summary. Other disks to watch can be added in the server's settings.
help-admin-problems-instrumentation-what: Live counters of what this WeKan server is doing: how many connections are open, and how often each method and publication is called, how often it fails and how long it takes. It shows which part of WeKan is busy or failing right now without a separate monitoring tool.
help-admin-problems-instrumentation-how-: The top line shows active, opened and closed connections and when counting started. Bars per area, such as Cards, Boards, Login or Attachments, show calls, average time and errors; click an area to show only its rows, and again to show all. The table lists calls, completed, errors, and average and maximum time. It refreshes every five seconds, counts only this server process, and starts again from zero on restart.
help-admin-problems-broken-cards-what-it: Lists cards that no board can show, because the board, swimlane or list they belong to is missing. It covers every board on the server, whether or not you are a member.
help-admin-problems-broken-cards-how-it-: Each row shows the card title, its id, the titles of the board, swimlane and list that still exist, its type and when it was created; an empty cell is the missing part. Type part of a title and press Enter to search, and page with the previous and next buttons. The pane only lists cards: repair them with Repair broken cards on Problems / Summary. Opening a board also repairs its own cards.
help-admin-problems-files-what-it-is-des: Lists the attachments stored on this server, with buttons that check what the database says about every attachment and avatar against what is really in storage. The checks find missing, unreferenced or mislabelled files and the history that may explain them.
help-admin-problems-files-how-it-works-d: The table shows a preview, file name, size, type and the ids of the attachment, board and card, with a search box. Check files and history, Check file types and extensions, or Check missing and untracked files starts a check; Cancel check stops it. Afterwards, read the counts, the coverage and the sample of findings, or use Download status summary. The checks never change, move or delete any file or record.
help-admin-problems-rules-what-it-is-des: Lists every automation rule on the server with its board, so you can see in one place what WeKan does automatically on all boards, for example when looking for a rule that moves cards unexpectedly.
help-admin-problems-rules-how-it-works-d: The table shows the rule title, its board, its action type and its trigger's activity type, 10 rows a page, sorted by board. Type part of a rule title and press Enter to search, and clear the box and press Enter to see all again. The pane is read-only: to change a rule, open its board and edit it in that board's rules.
